cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: arctangent of 1 in radians (pi/4)
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.785398163. Independently verified in Python: math.atan(1) = 0.7853981633974483, which is exactly pi/4 -> 0.785398163 at 9 dp

cases.description: The same example converted to degrees with the DEGREES function, as the page's third example does
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 45. Independently verified: pi/4 radians = 45 degrees exactly, and the double-precision conversion is exactly 45.0
tan(0) = 0 and the documented output range is -pi/2 to pi/2, which contains exactly one angle with tangent zero, so ATAN(0) = 0 exactly
#VALUE! is Excel's documented error for an argument of the wrong type; the ACOT page states it explicitly for this inverse-trigonometric family
